clue.text: Cast "least raunchy" West End farce

indicators.note: to cast is to mould afresh, so the quoted words are poured into a new shape

blocks.note: the quoted words supply all twelve letters

explanation.surface: A theatre company is cast for a West End farce billed as the least raunchy show in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as the actors, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement; CHARLEY'S AUNT is the long-running Victorian farce by Brandon Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: Charley's Aunt is a famous comedy of disguise first staged in London's theatre district in 1892.

clue.text: Fancy carafe filled with black coffee served here

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or made-up, so the vessel's letters are arranged fancifully
something filled with an item holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: An elegant carafe of black coffee is brought to the table at some smart venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'coffee served here' is the definition, describing a place rather than a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe bar is an establishment where customers order coffee as well as alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Appeared in A&E clutching mostly painful back

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped
going back means travelling the wrong way, so the shortened word is read right to left
to clutch is to hold tightly, so the hospital pair grip the other piece between them

blocks.note: the two letters of the hospital department's name, split around the middle
a sore spot is a painful one

explanation.surface: Someone turns up at the emergency department with a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is Accident and Emergency, the British hospital casualty department; 'painful back' looks like the patient's complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is a past tense meaning came into being or emerged, just as something that appeared did.

clue.text: Satirised light over 1D?

blocks.note: a lamp is a light
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
the cross-reference is read literally as 'one D'

explanation.surface: Something mocked appears to be a light hanging over the entry at 1 Down.
explanation.walkthrough: 1D looks like a pointer to the cafe bar clue, but it is simply read out as the number and letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon is to ridicule in satire, so lampooned is the past tense of that mockery.

clue.text: City known for its Rose Bowl

definitions.text: City known for its Rose Bowl

blocks.note: surface reading: a famous sports stadium, in Pasadena or Southampton
setter's reading: the English city whose royal house took the white rose as its emblem, and whose name lies inside a cricketer's delivery

explanation.walkthrough: The Rose Bowl pulls towards American football or Hampshire cricket. The white rose is the emblem of the House of York, and a yorker is a ball bowled at the batter's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city in northern England gave its name to the white-rose dynasty of the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Strong Greek unwell, chopping pines

indicators.note: chopping cuts into something, so one word splits the other open and sits inside it

blocks.note: to pine for something is to ache for it
unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A sturdy Greek woodsman, though feeling poorly, is felling pine trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' reads as trees to be chopped, but it is the verb meaning yearns.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was the mightiest Greek warrior at Troy in Homer's Iliad, invulnerable save for his heel.

clue.text: South African resident having lay over in North America

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned over means flipped end to end
in places one piece inside the abbreviation for the continent

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A South African living in North America has had a stopover there.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope native to southern Africa, so it is literally a resident of that region.

clue.text: Big Mac?

blocks.note: surface reading: the famous fast-food hamburger
setter's reading: mac is short for mackintosh, a raincoat, and a big one goes over everything else

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals push you towards McDonald's; a mac is the British word for a waterproof raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heavy coat worn on top of other clothes is what a large raincoat amounts to.

clue.text: Lounge around, wearing unlined bomber jacket

indicators.note: with the lining removed only the outer shell of the word survives
something being worn is wrapped around the wearer, so one piece is clothed in the other

blocks.note: just the first and last letters
to lounge around is to laze

explanation.surface: Someone idles about in a bomber jacket with the lining torn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bomber jacket' looks like one item of clothing, but the jacket is the definition and the bomber is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a tailored jacket, often worn as part of a school or club uniform.

clue.text: Push forwards and run through mist when winter ends

indicators.note: running through something passes inside it, so one letter goes into the word for haze

blocks.note: fog is thick mist
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the month in which winter is over and spring begins

explanation.surface: Someone is shoved ahead and made to run through the mist at the close of winter.
explanation.definitionFit: To frogmarch someone is to force them forward by holding their arms from behind.

clue.text: Smith's block that stops strike from The Hammers?

definitions.text: Smith's block that stops strike from The Hammers?

blocks.note: surface reading: a shot at goal by West Ham United, the football club nicknamed the Hammers
setter's reading: the iron block in a forge, which takes every blow of a blacksmith's hammer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smith' could be a goalkeeper blocking a shot from West Ham, the London club called the Hammers; really it is a blacksmith.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the heavy iron block on which a smith beats hot metal into shape.

clue.text: British run public school, one associated with special cap

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Eton College is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A British-run public school awards one pupil a special cap.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is a fee-paying private school; Eton is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Brittany is linked to the Breton cap, the flat-crowned fisherman's hat named after that region.

clue.text: Jailhouse Rock?

blocks.note: surface reading: the Elvis Presley song and film
setter's reading: a rocky island in San Francisco Bay, nicknamed The Rock, that held a federal prison

explanation.walkthrough: The title of the Elvis hit sends you to music; read literally it is a rock that is a jailhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The former maximum-security penitentiary on an island in San Francisco Bay was known as The Rock.

clue.text: Old master enthralled by Cherub en soleil

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so the name is held inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A great painter is captivated by a cherub basking in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'En soleil' is French for 'in the sun', apt for cherubs, which this painter painted in abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was a Flemish Baroque painter, one of the Old Masters of European art.

clue.text: I say nothing should be taken away from 80s pop icon

indicators.note: taking away means subtracting, so one character is removed from the name

blocks.note: the Culture Club singer famous in the 1980s
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An exclamation of protest that nobody should detract from a 1980s pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like the start of a sentence, but it is the definition: an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: By George is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise or emphasis, used like the British expression I say.

clue.text: Severely criticise Blue Boar cooking

indicators.note: cooking transforms the ingredients, and here also suggests cooking the books by rearranging them

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner slams the food at the Blue Boar, a typical English pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour someone is to attack them verbally at length, a figurative sense of beating.

clue.text: Nouveau riche thoroughfare in development of Riviera

indicators.note: a development is a change of form, so the resort's letters are rebuilt
in places the road inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A newly wealthy person buys a road in a property development on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is a social climber who has recently gained wealth or status, the same idea as an upstart.

clue.text: Punctilious individual beginning to solve tricky puzzle

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: the initial letter only
a tickler is a difficult or puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A fussy person sets about cracking a hard puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' tempts as an anagram signal, but the phrase is a definition of a teaser.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact correctness, so the word names a pedantic person.

clue.text: Female leaving a certain froideur, a sense of being inflexible

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: froideur is coldness of manner
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman walks out because of someone's coldness and stubbornness.
explanation.walkthrough: Froideur is French borrowed into English for chilly aloofness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigidity is stiffness, the quality of not bending or yielding.

clue.text: Teacher about to host a couple of bishops and religious scholars

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the title is read backwards
a host takes guests in, so the other letters go inside

blocks.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, twice

explanation.surface: A teacher is about to welcome two bishops and some theologians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher' tempts as the definition, since a rabbi is a teacher, but the plural answer needs 'religious scholars'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbis are Jewish scholars and teachers of religious law.

clue.text: Notorious Roman coach nursing depression

indicators.note: nursing something is cradling it, so the vehicle holds the hollow inside

blocks.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
a rut is a groove or hollow in the ground

explanation.surface: A trainer of some infamy is suffering from depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' and 'depression' suggest a sports trainer's mental health; both are concrete nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus is infamous as one of the assassins of Julius Caesar, his former friend.

clue.text: He calls people to order a piece of audio equipment

blocks.note: first meaning: the presiding officer of a legislature such as the House of Commons
second meaning: a loudspeaker

explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' sits between the halves so they read as one sentence about ordering a stereo part; the Commons chairperson famously shouts 'Order!'
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the chair of a parliamentary chamber and the device that converts signals into sound.

clue.text: Cable too tangled – it's tied in a knot

indicators.note: something tangled is twisted out of order, so these letters lie jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cable has got so snarled that it has ended up knotted.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootlace is the cord threaded through a boot's eyelets and fastened with a bow.

clue.text: Including tense, set down old language

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so the letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: lain is the past participle of lie, to be set down
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A grammar note: an ancient language is written out complete with its tenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin was the language of ancient Rome, no longer spoken as a mother tongue.

clue.text: Disclose six-shooter, unholstered

indicators.note: taken out of its holster, the gun loses its covering, so the outside letters go

blocks.note: a six-shooter is a revolver

explanation.surface: A gunslinger reveals a pistol, drawn from its holster.
explanation.walkthrough: Evolve has an older sense of unfold or reveal, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve originally meant to unroll or open out, hence to bring to light.

clue.text: Depart for holiday

blocks.note: first meaning: to go away
second meaning: time off work

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as setting off on vacation; 'holiday' is the British word for time off, as in annual leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for going away and the noun for authorised absence from work.

clue.text: Stare stupidly in interval, prodded by wife

indicators.note: prodding pokes into something, so the letter is pushed inside the gap word

blocks.note: a gap is an interval
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man gapes vacantly during the interval until his wife nudges him.
explanation.walkthrough: Gawp is British informal for gaping.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp is to gaze open-mouthed in a foolish way.

clue.text: Heavy metal bar?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pub where rock music fans drink
setter's reading: a weighty block of cast metal, such as gold

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the pun on a rock-music venue; read literally, it is a bar made of metal, and heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, typically gold or silver, shaped for storage.

clue.text: Unscrupulous lender reported single nurse?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so a word's sound counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: single means alone
the nurse shark is a species of shark

explanation.surface: A shady moneylender is said to be an unmarried nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' suggests a hospital worker; it is the bottom-dwelling nurse shark.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark is a moneylender charging extortionate interest, often backed by threats.

clue.text: Businessman agent/rep René Urtreger engages

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so the word lies held within the phrase

blocks.note: the letters span the slash and the pianist's name

explanation.surface: A businessman hired by an agent to represent the French jazz pianist René Urtreger.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepreneur sets up a business and takes on its financial risks.
